pages.description: Pan de Muerto, a Mexican sweet bread eaten for Día de los Muertos, is more than just a festive treat. Its history mirrors the holiday itself, a combination of cultures that breathes life back into the dead
pages.text: Mexico's Bread of the Dead Kneads Together Indigenous and Catholic Traditions Skip to main content Travel | October 30, 2026 Mexico’s Bread of the Dead Kneads Together Indigenous and Catholic Traditions Pan de Muerto, a Mexican sweet bread eaten for Día de los Muertos, is more than just a festive treat. Its history mirrors the holiday itself, a combination of cultures that breathes life back into the dead Pan de muerto is an orange-scented sweet bread traditionally prepared and eaten during Día de los Muertos , a Mexican holiday celebrated each year from October 31 to November 2. Eder Marcos Camacho Gomez/Getty Images Pan de muerto is an orange-scented sweet bread traditionally prepared and eaten during Día de los Muertos , a Mexican holiday celebrated each year from October 31 to November 2. Eder Marcos Camacho Gomez/Getty Images It’s autumn in Mexico City, and baker Elena Reygadas and her team at Panadería Rosetta are hard at work in the kitchen. Deftly, they shape mounds of soft, elastic dough into perfect rounds. Then, with two fingers, they gingerly form the huesitos , or little bones, laying the thin strips in a cross over the buns. A tray full of rolls slides into the bakery rack, resting alongside dozens of other matching loaves waiting for their turn in the oven. The bakers are making pan de muerto , an orange-scented sweet bread traditionally prepared and eaten during Día de los Muertos , Day of the Dead, a Mexican holiday celebrated each year from October 31 to November 2. For three days, legend decrees, the border between the mortal and spirit realms disappears.

Naval authorities began the search for the men, aged 53 and 32, after their fishing cooperative lost contact with them on 15 August and sent out a distress call. Close michaelIsADullGuy's Diary 南京新街口地块精细化更新日志 Posted by michaelIsADullGuy on 29 May 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . 前言 新街口作为南京乃至华东地区最重要的商业核心之一，其 OSM 数据长期存在建筑轮廓粗糙、地下空间缺失、路径拓扑混乱等问题。为此，我启动了一项针对新街口地块的系统性精细化更新计划，并在此记录操作步骤与我所制定的制图标准，供社区参考与讨论。 一、建筑物轮廓与属性细化 所有建筑物的轮廓均参照最新卫星影像与实地核查进行重新描绘或修正，具体标准如下： 轮廓贴合建筑基底，避免过度简化或偏移； 补充 building:levels 、 height 、 name 、 start_date 等属性； 对于综合体建筑（如德基广场、金鹰国际），区分裙楼与塔楼，分别以 building 、 building:part 进行三维建模。 二、地下商业空间的划定 新街口地铁站（地铁1号线×2号线换乘）向四周延伸出大量地下通道，直接连通周边各大商场的负一层。凡与地铁站地下通道 直接联通 的商场负一层空间，均按以下标准标注为地下建筑区域： 使用 location=underground 或 layer=-1 标记相关区域； 地下商业区域的范围多边形参照实际通道出入口与商业空间边界绘制； 与地铁站直接相连的通道本身，以 tunnel=yes + layer=-1 的 highway=footway 表示； 暂不确定是否联通的区域，暂以 fixme=需核实地下联通情况 标注，留待后续实地核查。 目前已完成地下空间划定的区域包括： 新街口百货商店 B1、金陵中环 B1 待补充区域： 金鹰国际购物中心 B1、德基广场 B1、中央商场 B1、南京国际金融中心 B1 等。 三、路径拓扑标准 这是本次更新中最容易出错的部分。为确保路网拓扑的清洁与导航规划的准确性，我制定了以下强制性规则： 3.1 各类道路不得混接 在主要路口， 行人路径（ highway=footway/pedestrian ）、自行车道（ highway=cycleway ）、机动车道（ highway=primary 等） 三者之间，原则上不建议建立直接连接节点，除非现实中存在明确的路权交汇点（如行人过街横道节点）。 3.2 跨图层要素禁止连接 任何两个 不属于同一 layer 值 的路径要素， 不得出现共享连接节点 ，以下情况除外： 允许连接的要素 说明 highway=steps 阶梯，连接不同楼层/层级 含 conveying=yes 的 highway=footway 自动扶梯 highway=elevator 电梯 除上述垂直交通要素外，地面路径与地下路径 一律不得出现连接点 。 此规则同样适用于在导航计算中看似”无害”的连接（例如建筑物轮廓与步行道路相切）。只要两个要素不属于同一图层，路径要素与非路径要素之间同样须保持几何上的独立性，仅在视觉上相邻即可。同一图层内的要素按正常规则连接，不受此限制。 如有异议或建议，欢迎在变更集评论或讨论页留言。 Happy mapping! 🗺️ Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

pages.title: Michelangelo Used These Custom, Multi-Headed Brushes While Painting 'The Last Judgment' to Replicate His Intricate Sculpting Techniques
pages.description: While restoring the Sistine Chapel, researchers discovered wavy groupings of brushstrokes which indicated that the artist used the special brushes to create a distinct crosshatching pattern
pages.text: Michelangelo Used These Custom, Multi-Headed Brushes While Painting 'The Last Judgment' to Replicate His Intricate Sculpting Techniques Skip to main content Detail showing the hair of one of the figures around Christ in The Last Judgment , as example of the use of a multi-tipped brush Governatorato SCV – Direzione dei Musei e dei Beni Culturali This spring, the Vatican restored the Sistine Chapel for the first time in 30 years. Restorers worked for three months to remove layers of calcium lactate—a whitish salt from the dried sweat from millions of visitors and the plaster in the walls—that had settled onto Michelangelo ’s immaculate 16th-century murals. As experts climbed temporary scaffolding and applied distilled water and absorbent Japanese paper to clean away the grime, they got a rare, close-up view of Michelangelo’s vivid masterpieces. They noticed something unique about The Last Judgment , the massive mural located behind the chapel’s altar, as its original colors emerged. Michelangelo had painted with wavy brushstrokes that appeared to have moved in synchronization. “I initially saw that Michelangelo painted with parallel strokes, often perpendicular to each to give a cross-hatching effect,” Paolo Violini , the Vatican’s chief restorer, tells the London Times ’ Tom Kington. “Then I saw that when a stroke wobbled slightly, other strokes parallel to it had an identical wobble. That meant one thing: Michelangelo was using special brushes with multiple heads, each with a small brush on the end of it, allowing him to produce parallel strokes with one large brush.” Examp

Most microbiomes contribute to necessary functions within us and our environments, like digestion and plant growth. We are largely living in successful partnership with them. A better understanding of these complex microbial communities would help us harness them for applications to human and animal health, agriculture and food safety, water treatment, manufacturing, renewable energy, and the detection of biological threats. For microbiome research to more quickly deliver products to the clinic and market and make the best use of taxpayer funding, the field requires standardized protocols for sample collection, and reference materials and data. These standardized tools help the many organizations working on microbiome research reproduce each other’s work and build upon it. SBA provides funds to specially designated intermediary lenders, which are nonprofit community-based organizations with experience in lending as well as management and technical assistance. These intermediaries administer the Microloan program for eligible borrowers. Am I eligible? A few weeks ago I wrote here about Wandering Around , a free browser game in which you can walk through any town or city on Earth, built on the fly from OpenStreetMap. Thanks to your comments and feedback, the game has now left beta: version 1.0 is live. Play it here: https://wanderingaround.games (phone and desktop, no download, no account needed) This post is about what changed on the OSM side since then. Buildings that look like the real thing Churches are built from their real outline. The game reads the shape of the building and finds the nave, the transepts and the choir, and each part gets its own roof that follows the shape. A square part that sticks out becomes the tower. A church mapped carefully as a cross shape now also looks like one at eye level. Mosques get a dome on a drum, pointed windows and a minaret. They are recognised by religion=muslim , building=mosque or the name. Cemeteries ( landuse=cemetery ) are laid out with gravel paths, rows of graves in neutral shapes, low hedges and trees. Sidewalks now run along the whole street as one continuous strip. Short gaps are filled and corners join neatly. Shop fronts, front doors and porches get their own place in the facade, so windows don’t end up behind a door. I’ve been building Wandering Around , a free browser game in which you can walk around any town or city on Earth. The whole world comes from OpenStreetMap, so I’d like to share how it uses OSM data and ask this community for feedback. Play it here: https://wanderingaround.games (works on phone and desktop, no account needed) News and updates: https://ko-fi.com/wanderingaroundtheworld Screenshots and a short video: https://mikehur.itch.io/wandering-around How the map is built Streets, buildings, water, parks and bridges come from OpenFreeMap vector tiles (zoom 14, OpenMapTiles schema). The game fetches the tiles around the player, decodes them in the browser, stitches buildings that are split across tile edges and turns everything back into OSM-style features with tags. The game logic works on those tags, so it is the same code whether the data comes from tiles or (as a fallback) from Overpass. 2D and 3D: the same data drives a 2D map and a 3D eye-level view. Building heights come from OSM where they are tagged. Transit: train routes and stations, city buses, ferries and signposts come from Overpass queries, so you can travel between real stops and stations. pages.text: Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors Under the Fair Labor Standards Act | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors Under the Fair Labor Standards Act A worker is entitled to minimum wage and overtime pay protections under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) when there is an employment relationship between the worker and an employer and there is coverage under the FLSA. Employers are responsible for determining whether a worker is an employee under the FLSA. Misclassification occurs when an employer treats a worker who is an employee under the FLSA as an independent contractor. Misclassifying employees as independent contractors is a serious problem because misclassified employees may not receive the minimum wage and overtime pay to which they are entitled under the FLSA or other benefits and protections to which they are entitled under the law. As part of its efforts to address misclassification, the Wage and Hour Division on January 10, 2024 published a final rule , effective March 11, 2024, revising its guidance on how to analyze whether a worker is an employee or independent contractor under the FLSA. This guidance is available in the form of regulations at 29 CFR Part 795. Employers and workers may consult these regulations and the additional resources listed below to help analyze a worker’s status as an employee or independent contractor under the FLSA. Mission The Office of Enterprise Assessments supports the Secretary of Energy and other stakeholders by enhancing the Department of Energy’s safety, security, and cybersecurity programs. We do this through independently evaluating the effectiveness of requirements, performance, and risk management; conducting objective and effective enforcement activities; and providing high-quality training. EA is organizationally independent of the DOE entities that develop and implement security and safety policy and programs. Therefore, EA can objectively provide information to DOE senior leadership, contractor organizations, and other stakeholders on whether the Department's national security assets are appropriately protected and Departmental operations provide for the safety of employees and the public. EA activities complement, but do not replace, the responsibility of DOE line management to ensure compliance with security and safety requirements. EA assessment activities evaluate whether the Department is effective in promoting robust protection strategies and making informed risk management decisions. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Missouri Breaks Interpretive Center Welcome to the Missouri Breaks Interpretive Center in Fort Benton, Montana—your gateway to understanding the rich cultural and natural history of the Upper Missouri River Breaks National Monument . Here, you can explore the powerful story of the Missouri River, a lifeline that has shaped the landscape and the people who have lived along its banks for thousands of years. Through engaging exhibits, visitors learn about the river’s role in westward expansion, from the awe-inspiring journey of Lewis and Clark to the bustling steamboat era that made Fort Benton the “world’s innermost port.” The center also sheds light on the region’s deeper stories—from the Nez Perce fleeing from the U.S. Army in 1877 to ancient paddlefish and sturgeon that still swim in its waters. Exhibits highlight the lives of Native peoples, early settlers, and the diverse wildlife that call the monument home. Hands-on displays, educational programs, and a riverside walking trail offer visitors of all ages a chance to connect with the land, history, and ongoing conservation of this remarkable stretch of the Missouri River. Monitoring Surface Water Chemistry Surface water chemistry is a direct indicator of the effects of acid rain on water bodies. Networks that monitor surface water chemistry over long time periods provide valuable information on aquatic ecosystem health and how water bodies respond to changes in acid-causing emissions. EPA oversees the Long-Term Monitoring (LTM) program, which tracks changes in surface water chemistry in response to changing air pollution and acid deposition. The goal of this long-term program is to track whether the Clean Air Act Amendments (CAAA) ( Plain English Guide to the Clean Air Act ) have been effective in reducing the acidity of surface waters in New England, the Northern Adirondack Mountains, Appalachian Plateau, and the Central Appalachians and advance the science of air pollution impacts on water resources. What are Acidified Surface Waters? Acid precipitation (commonly known as acid rain) primarily affects sensitive bodies of water, which are located in watersheds whose soils have a limited ability to neutralize acidic compounds (called “buffering capacity”). pages.text: Mortality Disparities in American Communities (MDAC) Mortality Disparities in American Communities (MDAC) Skip Navigation Mortality Disparities in American Communities (MDAC) Project Overview Data Availability Research Proposal Reference Manual Bibliography More Sponsors and Investigators Limitations & Confidentiality Project Overview Project Overview Data Availability Research Proposal Reference Manual Bibliography Sponsors and Investigators Limitations & Confidentiality Project Overview Project Description The MDAC is a study developed to permit research on social, economic, demographic, and occupational differentials in mortality. These objectives are achieved through record linkage of the large, nationally representative, 2008 American Community Survey (ACS) with mortality outcomes derived from the National Death Index (NDI) housed at the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) and Medicare/Medicaid information obtained from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). This wilderness encompasses an eight-mile-long stretch of the central (and highest) portion of the Black Mountains. Nutt Mountain, at 5,216 feet, presides over a colorful and wild terrain. Along the main ridgeline, prominent mesas have been cut into a series of steep maze-like canyons. Outward from the main ridgeline, numerous huge volcanic plugs ring the entire wilderness. pages.description: The musician and actor on being stranded alone in Mexico and why travelling with her band is like being part of a circus.
pages.text: Musician Kate Nash on Her Irish Heritage and the Reality of Touring | National Geographic TRAVEL Musician Kate Nash on Her Irish Heritage and the Reality of Touring The musician and actor on being stranded alone in Mexico and why travelling with her band is like being part of a circus. Kate Nash is a singer, songwriter and actress from London. Ellius Grace As told to Flora Neighbour Published November 15, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (U K). Flora Neighbour: Your new album is influenced by your Irish heritage. Did a particular place inspire one of the songs? Kate Nash: My family are from Galway, Sligo and Cavan, so I really wanted to explore these places in my artistry. But the track Christmas Eve is actually about my granny and grandad meeting on O’Connell Street in Dublin on Christmas Eve. I’ll always have an affinity with Dublin as that’s where their journey started. FN: What do you hope people will take from the album? KN: It’s quite a dense record, with some heavy topics, but I want it to be empowering. I also hope that people feel a lot of happiness. Irish music is innately joyful, so I hope it’s uplifting to listen to as well as quite emotional. Nowadays, people are much more open to exploring their heritage, so I think now’s the right time to release this music. FN: Where should everyone visit while in Ireland? KN: I’d send people to the west coast and tell them to drive up the Wild Atlantic Way. Visit Spiddal in Galway, as it has great places to eat and drink. There’s somewhere right next to my studio, actually, called Builín Blast
